pages.heading: Run code only when a condition is true
pages.body: A condition is a yes-or-no question. An if statement runs its indented or braced block only when that question is true. Compare numbers with >, <, >= and <=. At least means >=; at most means <=.

pages.heading: Choose one path
pages.body: Use else for the alternative. Add elif to check more cases in order. The first true branch runs, so put the highest threshold first when comparing scores or temperatures.

pages.heading: Combine and invert conditions
pages.body: AND (and) requires both conditions. OR (or) accepts either. NOT (not) reverses true and false. Boolean values use True and False.

pages.heading: Put a decision inside another
pages.body: Nested if statements let one decision lead to another. First decide who the user is, then decide what that user may do. Keep each nested block indented clearly. Run your code freely, and Submit when the exact output matches the mission.

boss.name: The Router
boss.prompt: The Router needs a safe route. battery is 80, hasBadge is true and networkOnline is false. First use AND to allow access only when battery is at least 50 and hasBadge is true. If access is denied, print "Access denied" only. If access is allowed, print "Access granted", then use a nested if/else to print "Online route" when networkOnline is true or "Backup route" otherwise. Use these variables; print each message on its own line.

hints.text: There are two decisions: grant access, then choose an online or backup route. With the given values, access is allowed and the backup route is needed.
Combine battery >= 50 with hasBadge using and. Put the networkOnline decision inside that successful branch.
Start with if battery >= 50 and hasBadge: and print "Access granted". Inside it, use if/else on networkOnline.
